t.E311.agn: In 2015 EFSA stated that the available data were too limited to set an acceptable daily intake (ADI) and that sufficient toxicological data were needed for a reliable evaluation. Because these data were not provided, the substance was removed from the EU authorised list in 2018.
t.E311.body: Gallate esters are broken down to gallic acid in the body (in the intestinal wall and also by gut bacteria). Most of the gallic acid is converted to 4-O-methylgallic acid and excreted in the urine, either free or conjugated with glucuronic acid.
t.E311.eff.0.t: It could not be evaluated owing to a lack of sufficient toxicological data; it was removed from the EU authorised list in 2018
t.E311.eval: No longer authorised as a food additive in the EU: it was removed from the authorised list by Regulation (EU) 2018/1481 (in 2015 EFSA did not find data to evaluate its safety).
t.E311.found.0: Not authorised in the EU since 2018
t.E311.prod: Produced by the chemical reaction of gallic acid with alcohols.
t.E311.regx.0: Re-evaluated; data insufficient to set an ADI, additional toxicological data needed for a full evaluation.
t.E311.regx.1: Removed from the EU list of authorised food additives by Commission Regulation (EU) 2018/1481; no business operator committed to providing the required toxicological data. A transition period was granted for products already placed on the market.
t.E311.summary: A synthetic antioxidant derived from gallic acid. It delays rancidity in fats and is used in fats and fatty products.
t.E311.what: It was an antioxidant that delayed the oxidation and rancidity of fats; it is no longer authorised in the EU.
